text:
ravi: Heads-up — EU-west1 observability spike: preemptions + network congestion causing cascade of tiny-gang + tiny-pod evictions. ~30% increase in evictions over last 20m.

olivia-sre: saw alert. graphs show interconnect egress saturation on rack-3 (eu-west1b), aligns with batch jobs starting.

mike_infra: are these on Dedicated or spot nodes? if spot, preemptions expected but NIC thrash is odd.

ravi: mostly spot-backed GPU pools; a couple Dedicated pinned. scheduler-bot: "evict_wave: detected 48 pod evictions in 15m, avg delay 2.1s" :warning:

scheduler-bot: "top offenders by label: tenant=training, workload=gpu-batch, affinity=prefer-same-rack"

elaine-ml: that 'prefer-same-rack' is the culprit — we packed many batches into one rack. when NIC egress saturates, scheduler keeps locality and evicts elsewhere.

samir-platform: quick mitigations: 1) relax rack affinity for tenant=training 2) widen preempt window to desynchronize evicts 3) scale warm pool in eu-west1c to absorb spill

olivia-sre: +1 warm pool. also can we gate large submissions at admission-controller when rack NIC > 80%?

mike_infra: I can patch admission-controller: if egress_per_rack > 75% deny-large-gang with 30s backoff. UX hit though.

ops-oncall: rolling canary: disabling prefer-same-rack for label workload=gpu-batch in eu-west1 for 10m, will monitor evictions.

ravi: please avoid mass cross-AZ reschedules; that increases network churn. prefer local fallback to smaller variants if available.

elaine-ml: can we tie model fallback to egress throttle? Redwood Optimize could surface lower-throughput variants automatically.

samir-platform: longer term: scheduler should mark racks with high egress as "soft-taint" and apply score penalty instead of immediate eviction.

mike_infra: raised INF-2026 "soft-taint by egress-pressure". linking grafana: grafana/d/rack-network?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now

olivia-sre: after canary disable, evictions down ~60% in 12m. rack-3 NIC still high but cascade reduced.

ops-oncall: leaving canary disabled 30m, will re-enable only after warm pool stable.

ravi: cost note — warm pool autoscale increases reserved GPU spend; finance check please for delta.

samir-platform: moving some batch to eu-west2 could be cheaper and add ~40ms customer latency, tradeoff worth evaluating.

mike_infra: mitigation checklist: 1) gate admissions at 75% egress 2) disable prefer-same-rack canary 3) spin warm pool eu-west1c 4) INF-2026 5) finance delta

ravi: thanks. keep updates short. post if evictions spike or warm pool healthy.

olivia-sre: update @ravi @mike_infra — warm pool up, +8 GPUs, evictions normalized. will close canary in 20m if stable. :thumbsup:

scheduler-bot: "evict_wave resolved: 3 evictions in last 10m" :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: closing oncall action after 45m. tracking INF-2026 in sprint planning.
